name: Workhuman
desc: Sells cloud-based human capital management software, including social recognition and rewards tools for employees.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.1bn (EUR 1.01bn) in 2022, up 29% on 2021, per director's report
markets: Headquartered in Dublin and Framingham, Massachusetts; sells recognition software to large employers in Europe and North America.
rationale: Global HR-tech brand selling to multinational employers; F1 hospitality and employee-experience storytelling could reach enterprise HR buyers.

name: SafetyCulture
desc: Australian company providing workplace safety, inspection and operations software tools used by frontline teams.
capacity_detail: Raised USD 73M in May 2021 at USD 1.6bn valuation, bringing total equity raised to about USD 180M
markets: Australia-based software sold to frontline businesses; investors include Insight Partners, Tiger Global, Index Ventures and Blackbird.
rationale: Safety and inspection software fits F1's engineering and operational-excellence story; B2B brand could use team partnerships for enterprise reach.

name: Souche
industry: used-car trading platform and dealer software
desc: Runs an online used-car trading platform in China linking most medium and large second-hand car dealerships.
capacity_detail: USD 578M Series F in 2018 brought total equity raised to more than USD 1.2bn (investors incl. Primavera, Morningside, Alibaba)
markets: China: online platform serving second-hand car dealerships, plus car leasing, logistics and dealer ERP software.
rationale: Automotive retail platform whose dealer and car-buyer audience overlaps with F1's growing Chinese fan base around the Shanghai Grand Prix.

name: ZBJ.com
desc: Chongqing-based online marketplace connecting businesses with freelancers for design, programming, marketing and other professional services.
capacity_detail: Series C of CNY 2.6bn (USD 419M) in June 2015 plus USD 18M Series B in 2014; total funding listed as USD 454M
markets: China: online platform serving small and medium businesses with design, software, IP, marketing and finance services.
rationale: SME-services platform seeking brand visibility before a Hong Kong listing; F1's China audience offers business-owner reach.

name: Tongdun Technology
desc: Chinese fintech company providing online risk-control and anti-fraud software to financial, insurance, payment and e-commerce firms.
capacity_detail: Rounds added: USD 72.8M Series C (Oct 2017, incl. Temasek) plus USD 100M Series D (Apr 2019) = USD 172.8M, plus an undisclosed D+ round
markets: China: serves banks, insurers, payment providers, online shopping and social networking companies with risk-control services.
rationale: B2B risk-control brand selling to financial institutions; F1 hospitality could support enterprise sales, but consumer brand value is limited.

name: Bucketplace
desc: Operates Ohouse (Oneului Jip), a South Korean online interior design community and home-furnishing commerce platform.
capacity_detail: Raised KRW 230bn (about USD 180M) in May 2022, led by Korea Development Bank with SoftBank Ventures, BOND and others
markets: South Korea: online interior content, home-furnishing e-commerce and renovation services; 2025 revenue KRW 321.5bn.
rationale: Consumer home brand with large Korean audience; F1 association could lift brand awareness if it expands overseas.

name: YunQuNa
desc: China-based digital logistics platform offering international land, air and sea freight, warehousing and customs services.
capacity_detail: USD 150M Series D1 in June 2021 led by CITIC Capital and Xianghe Capital; about USD 300M raised in total
markets: China-based cross-border shipping with branches in the US, Brazil, Japan and Thailand; plans for further overseas regions.
rationale: Cross-border logistics firm building an overseas network; F1's global freight-heavy calendar offers a credible logistics storytelling platform.

name: Kendra Scott
desc: Austin-based fashion jewellery and accessories brand selling through its own US stores and online.
capacity_detail: More than USD 500M in annual sales (Glossy, Dec 2025; figure not attributed to the company); 168 US stores
markets: United States: 168 own stores, expanding on the West Coast, Northeast and Midwest, plus e-commerce and Yellow Rose sub-brand.
rationale: Fast-growing US accessible-luxury brand targeting women; F1's growing young female US audience (Austin GP host city) fits its customer.
theme: Consumer brands: beauty, fashion, food & drink
